pages.text:
Everyone knows that
Khuzwayo loves to dance.
When the village leader
chooses him to be the
next Ingoma dancer, no
one is surprised.
pages.change: Khuzwayo, known for loving to dance, is chosen as the next Ingoma dancer
pages.page_turn_note: A statement page; the turn explains what Ingoma is.

notes: eyes closed and smiling, he dances barefoot beside a radio with music notes floating around
illustration.only_in_image: He dances along to a portable radio: his everyday dancing is to recorded music at home, not the ceremony the text names.

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.text:
Ingoma is a dance to
celebrate the first crops at
the beginning of the year.
Khuzwayo's family is proud.
pages.change: Ingoma is explained as a harvest dance and his family is proud
pages.page_turn_note: Calm exposition; the turn brings the 'But'.

notes: a pale blue cloud holds three grown dancers with sticks and grass skirts; an adult's hand rests on Khuzwayo's shoulder
illustration.only_in_image: The pale cloud of grown dancers is what he pictures: the adult performers he must now join, and an adult's hand on his shoulder stands for the family's pride.

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.text:
But Khuzwayo is worried.
How will he dance in front of
so many people
from so many villages?
He normally only performs for
a few neighbours.
pages.change: He is worried: he has danced only for a few neighbours, never for many villages
pages.question_created: How will he dance in front of so many people?
pages.page_turn_note: The text asks his question directly; the answer comes as flight after the turn.

notes: he stands very small in the middle of a mostly white spread, hands clasped, with a worried mouth and sweat drops
illustration.only_in_image: He is drawn tiny in a large empty page: the scale shows how small he feels before the crowd the text describes.

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.text:
"I can't do it!
It's too scary."
He
runs
away ...
pages.change: He says it is too scary and runs away
pages.page_turn_note: The words step down the page and grow larger toward an ellipsis; his legs and a dust cloud leave the right edge exactly where the reader turns.

notes: only his legs and a dust cloud are visible at the right edge; the words descend like footsteps
illustration.only_in_image: He is already half off the right edge of the page in a dust cloud: the picture makes him leave the spread at the page turn.

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.text:
Everyone wonders where he is.
No one can find him.
But Khuzwayo's best friends
know exactly where he would be!
pages.change: No one can find him, but his two best friends know where he would be
pages.page_turn_note: The friends know and the reader does not; the turn shows the place without words.

notes: a woman lifts a basket lid, a man peers over bushes; the friends grin and point at each other
illustration.only_in_image: The adults search in silly places (inside a basket, over a bush) while the two friends, a girl in pink and a boy in blue, exchange knowing looks: who the friends are is only in the picture.

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.change: Without words, the friends find him sitting alone in the maize field
pages.page_turn_note: A wordless reveal; the turn brings the friends' question.

notes: full-bleed maize field; the two friends peek through the stalks one above the other; Khuzwayo sits on the ground looking down
illustration.only_in_image: Where he went and that he sits alone and downcast in the maize field are told only by the picture; the page has no words.

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.change: A friend asks why he ran away
pages.page_turn_note: A direct question answered after the turn.

notes: the girl gestures as she asks; the boy has his arm around Khuzwayo, who looks at the ground
illustration.only_in_image: The boy friend has an arm around his shoulders while he looks down; the comfort is shown, not said, and the speaker is identified only by her gesture.

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.text:
"I am nervous.
What if I make
a mistake?"
pages.change: He names his feeling: he is nervous of making a mistake
pages.question_created: What if he makes a mistake?
pages.page_turn_note: His own question hangs; the friends answer it after the turn.

notes: sweat drops; hands wringing at his chest; the girl's hand reaches toward his arm
illustration.only_in_image: The girl reaches out to touch his arm as he speaks.

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.text:
"We can help you.
Let's all practise together!"
"Khuzwayo, you're so good. You're
ready to dance with the older dancers!"
pages.change: The friends offer to practise with him and, as they dance, tell him he is ready for the older dancers
pages.page_turn_note: Resolution in progress; no open question.

notes: all three kick their legs high in the maize field in a cloud of dust
illustration.only_in_image: They practise in the very maize field where he hid: the hiding place becomes the rehearsal space.

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.page_turn_note: A short statement; the turn jumps to the day itself.

notes: he dances smiling among the legs of much taller dancers whose upper bodies are cut off by the page
illustration.only_in_image: He is already dancing among the much bigger older dancers, still small beside them but smiling: the practice the text skips is shown.

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.text:
On the day of the
Ingoma dance
Khuzwayo leads his
village to the arena
wearing a special outfit.
He still feels a little
nervous, but the
rattles on his feet
guide him.
pages.change: On the day he leads his village to the arena in costume, still a little nervous, steadied by the rattles on his feet
pages.page_turn_note: The approach to the performance; the turn shows the dance itself.

notes: in grass skirt and headband with a stick, he walks ahead; his two friends and faded adult figures follow
illustration.only_in_image: His two friends walk right behind him in the procession, among the faded adults.

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.text:
He stomps his legs.
He waves his arms.
Everyone loves
Khuzwayo's dance!
pages.change: He stomps and waves and everyone loves his dance
pages.page_turn_note: Last story spread; the book closes with an unworded vignette.

notes: raised hands of the crowd fill the bottom; faded adult dancers behind him; the words grow larger line by line

pages.label: OBSERVED
